title: Kestrel Care Vehicle Service Contract Training Note: When a Plan Expires
content:
**Rule.** A Kestrel Care Vehicle Service Contract plan expires on its expiration date or when the odometer passes its expiration odometer, whichever comes first; repairs begun before expiration and authorized are still paid.

Each plan carries two end points, both written on the plan: the expiration date, which is the date its time term ends, and the expiration odometer, which is the odometer at purchase plus the miles of coverage of its mileage term. An active plan expires at whichever of the two is reached first; the expiration is recorded by the system and the expiration date on the plan is not changed by it.

## Questions answered by the rule

**Which end point governs?** Whichever comes first. A plan driven heavily can expire on mileage long before its expiration date; a plan driven lightly expires on its expiration date with the odometer still below its expiration odometer.

**What happens to a repair that was under way at expiration?** A repair begun before expiration and authorized is still paid after the plan has expired.

## Hypothetical cases

| Expiration date | Expiration odometer | Event that comes first | Plan expires |
|---|---|---|---|
| A date three years ahead | 80000 miles | The odometer passes 80000 miles in the second year | When the odometer passes 80000 miles |
| A date three years ahead | 80000 miles | The expiration date arrives with the odometer at 61000 miles | On the expiration date |

A repair begun and authorized in the week before the plan's expiration date, and completed after it, is still paid.
